inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR. Risk-free ~6.7% (India 10-year G-sec), equity risk premium ~6.5% (mature-market premium plus India country risk), beta ~1.15 for an integrated steel cyclical gives cost of equity ~14.2%. Pre-tax rupee/blended debt cost ~8.5%, ~6.4% after tax, at a ~25% target debt weight (rating-agency debt including acceptances): WACC ~12.2%, rounded to 12.0%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios; cyclicality, China dumping and execution risk are carried in the flows and the weights, not in the rate. Terminal growth 4.5% is INR nominal, well under the risk-free rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A (leases as debt). Reported EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116, so lease cost is not in the flows; lease liabilities of Rs 3,569 crore (3,127 non-current + 442 current, 30 Sep 2026) are deducted once in equity_bridge. No lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI deducted once in equity_bridge at book, Rs 169 crore at 30 Sep 2026 (it fell from Rs 5,422 crore at 31 Mar 2026 once the BPSL/Piombino structure unwound). Immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build, Drivers route) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations. JSW Steel is an operating company whose value is unlevered free cash flow; first valuation of this ticker, no prior model. ONE-OFF TRAP: FY2026 statutory PAT of Rs 25,508 crore (Rs 22,316 crore attributable, EPS 91.25) includes an Rs 18,051 crore exceptional gain on loss of control of the Bhushan Power & Steel (BPSL) steel business, transferred on 27 Mar 2026 into a 50:50 JV with JFE Steel. Nothing in this model is built from FY2026 net income or FY2026 FCF: the flows are rebuilt from revenue x operating EBITDA margin (which excludes other income, JV share and exceptionals). FY2026 reported FCF of Rs 10,498 crore is also not a run-rate: it is before interest paid (Ind AS puts ~Rs 9,000 crore of interest in financing), it includes a full year of BPSL, and capex of Rs 14,654 crore is stepping up to Rs 22,000-24,000 crore guided for FY2027. BASE REVENUE: FY2026 revenue of Rs 185,470 crore includes BPSL until 27 Mar 2026; year-1 growth is anchored to H1 FY2027 actual revenue of Rs 101,850 crore (ex-BPSL) and the 28.6 Mt sales guidance, so the deconsolidation is already inside the year-1 rate. MID-CYCLE: H1 FY2027 operating EBITDA margin was 19.15% against 16.1% in FY2026 and a FY2018-FY2026 average of ~18.6% (range 11.2%-26.6%); the base case fades to 17.0%, not the current print. ACCEPTANCES: Rs 20,537 crore of interest-bearing supplier-finance acceptances are treated as debt (deducted in equity_bridge), as rating agencies do; the company's own net debt excludes them and their interest sits in finance cost, so leaving them in working capital would charge that financing nowhere. Working-capital capture is therefore set on trade working capital excluding acceptances. NON-OPERATING ASSETS: operating EBITDA excludes JV/associate profit and other income, so the matching assets are added in equity_bridge (JSW JFE Kalinga stake, other JVs/associates, non-current investments). SBC is tiny (0.09% of revenue), so house and street values nearly coincide. Share count flat. Not modelled: the pending CCI cartel finding (penalty exposure up to 10% of turnover, contested) and the proposed BMM Ispat amalgamation (related party; CCI approved 6 Oct 2026, other approvals pending) which may issue shares.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: volume-led (36.4 -> 50 MTPA domestic capacity by FY2030) at flat real prices; NOT equity_5yr_cagr
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (15-17%) and EPS CAGR (23-75%) are both inflated by the Rs 18,051 crore FY2026 exceptional gain and diverge by far more than 30% from the 3-year revenue CAGR of 3.8%. On normalised FY2026 PAT of ~Rs 8,700 crore (EPS ~36) the 5-year EPS CAGR is ~2% and the 3-year ~28% off a trough FY2023. The 5-year revenue CAGR starts from a COVID-depressed FY2021. None of these is a usable growth anchor; the driver path is built from the capacity roadmap instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; no interest-income strip because the company carries net debt). Reported and owner FCF CAGRs are indistinguishable because SBC is ~0.1% of revenue. Reported FCF here is before interest paid, which Ind AS classifies in financing.

base.rationale: Year 1 (FY2027): H1 actual revenue Rs 101,850 crore and Q2 run-rate imply ~Rs 208,500 crore, +12.5% on the BPSL-inclusive FY2026 base; H1 margin 19.15%, Q2 18.57% with coking coal up $12-15/t, so 18.3% for the year. Capex 11% is the Rs 22,000-24,000 crore guidance. Years 2-5 revenue follows volume from 28.6 Mt toward ~41 Mt as Dolvi Phase III (Sept 2027), JVML +5 MTPA and Utkal Phase 1 come on, at roughly flat nominal prices after the FY2027 uplift. Capex over years 1-5 sums to ~Rs 126,000 crore, matching the approved pipeline. Margin fades to a 17.0% mid-cycle (about Rs 12,000 EBITDA/t), below the nine-year average of 18.6% because industry capacity additions are outrunning downstream demand. Terminal capex 6.0% against D&A 4.3% funds 4.5% nominal growth. Cash tax ramps to the 25.2% statutory rate as accelerated depreciation on the build fades. Working capital consumes 13% of incremental revenue (inventory + receivables - trade payables is ~15% of sales; acceptances are in the debt bridge).

scenario_narratives.base: India's steel demand grows 7-8% a year and JSW delivers its approved pipeline roughly on time: domestic capacity reaches 50 MTPA by FY2030 and sales volume rises from 28.6 Mt to about 41 Mt. Realisations stay near FY2027 levels in nominal terms. The 19% margin of H1 FY2027 does not hold: coking coal costs and about 26 Mt of new industry capacity pull EBITDA back to a 17% mid-cycle (around Rs 12,000/t), with the richer value-added mix and captive ore offsetting only part of that. Capex of roughly Rs 126,000 crore over five years absorbs most of the operating cash flow until FY2031, after which capex falls toward 6% of revenue and free cash flow opens up.
scenario_narratives.bull: Safeguard duties hold and are broadened, Chinese exports ease, and Indian demand runs at 9%+. New capacity fills quickly, the value-added share moves past 65% (CRGO electrical steel, automotive AHSS), and captive iron ore and Illawarra/Mozambique coking coal reach ~50% of need. EBITDA margin settles at 20% (about Rs 14,500/t), close to the FY2018-FY2019 level but below the FY2021-FY2022 peak. Brownfield cost of $550-600/t keeps capex intensity no higher than base despite faster growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: China's surplus keeps flowing into Asia, safeguard duties are diluted or circumvented (imports were already up 29.5% in April-August 2026), and domestic capacity additions outrun demand. Prices fall in FY2028 and margin drops to 13-14%, the FY2023/FY2025 level, recovering only to 15%. JSW is mid-build and cannot stop: capex stays above 10% of revenue for two more years while EBITDA shrinks, free cash flow is negative in FY2028-FY2029 and leverage rises again. Later projects are deferred, so growth is slower. A CCI cartel penalty would come on top and is not in these flows.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the company is committed to a debt-funded build at the point in the cycle where margins are above average, and both of the last two downturns (FY2023, FY2025) took margin to 11-14% within a year. Base 50%: the capacity roadmap is approved, funded and brownfield-heavy, and a 17% margin sits inside the range of seven of the last nine years. Bull cut to 25%: it needs trade protection to hold, Chinese exports to ease and new domestic capacity to be absorbed, three things outside management's control.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value is the unlevered cash flow of a first-quartile-cost steelmaker through a full cycle, after paying for the capacity that produces the growth. Three things are deliberately not capitalised: the FY2026 exceptional gain, the above-average H1 FY2027 margin, and FY2026 reported free cash flow (pre-interest, BPSL-inclusive, pre capex step-up). The market price implies roughly 10x EV/EBITDA on FY2027 earnings that are themselves above mid-cycle; the model's terminal value is about 6x mid-cycle EBITDA, in line with where integrated steelmakers have been valued across cycles. The gap between price and value is mostly that multiple, not a disagreement about volumes.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin is the dominant driver: each 1pp of EBITDA margin held across all years and the terminal value is worth roughly Rs 95-100 per share in the base case
Capex intensity after FY2031: the model assumes capex falls to 6% of revenue; a move to the 78 MTPA FY2032 ambition would keep free cash flow low for longer (and add volume)
Discount rate: at a 10-11% WACC, which Indian sell-side models commonly use, the base value rises to about Rs 640-710 per share, still roughly half the price (see required_return_table)
Acceptances treated as debt deduct about Rs 84 per share relative to the company's own net-debt definition
JSW JFE Kalinga stake is valued off JFE's entry price less 20% (about Rs 52 per share); there is no market quote
CCI cartel finding (penalty up to 10% of turnover or 3x profit) and the BMM Ispat related-party amalgamation are not modelled
Rupee depreciation raises imported coking coal cost and the rupee value of dollar debt
